barCharacter: Liam de Lioncourt. His comic job is closest: a formal, status-conscious snob whose pose keeps leaking a lonely, earnest dork, which is exactly Prince (lavish royal who only wants a reply). Vera (money, status, every line an ask) and Miranda (royal, courtly, brutal stakes) are adjacent; Miranda has too few lines in the corpus to field twelve.

headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Cover the names AND the mail vocabulary and Liam is still Liam: formal subordinate clauses (supposing I were to, we have indeed encountered), 'friend', hyperbole collapsing into a plea. Prince's identity lives in his nouns (junk, unsubscribe, attachment, URGENT), not his syntax. Nine of our twelve are two to four clipped full-stop declaratives, which is the cast's house shape: strip 'spam folder' and 'reply' and these read as Crumb or Nav. Only the header lines (Subject:, Dear Valued Customer, Fwd:) are Prince by shape.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours. Our twelve average about 12 words, every one turns on its last two to five words, nothing explains itself. Liam's set runs 15 to 27 words, and #27 and #31 have no turn at all. But across the whole bank the turn is mechanised: a two-word deflating tag after a full stop (Purely decorative. Minor one. Brave. Frankly, suspicious.) fires about a dozen times.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Ours. 'I am marking it unread so I can open it again', 'the drafts folder, where I am perfect', 'It looked underdressed. I added a fee' and 'My password. Everyone else asks for yours' are clip-able. Liam's corpus gives two (#10, #26), and his best laugh (#30) belongs to the player.
headToHead.overall: The bar wins. Prince's best lines are better jokes than Liam's, but Liam is a better written CHARACTER: his voice is a grammar, Prince's is a glossary. Ours is not at least as good on voice, so ours cannot win.

biggestGap: Prince is written in the cast's house telegram (two or three clipped declaratives plus a two-word deflating tag), so his voice is a vocabulary of mail words, not a sentence shape; the persona promises a lavish, breathless spam email. Next pass: rewrite a third of the bank as ONE long over-courteous spam sentence with stacked formal clauses (I am writing to inform you, with the deepest respect and at no cost to yourself, that...) whose last two to four words are the small human want, and cut the post-full-stop adjective tag to three uses in the whole bank.
